paper.title: Simple regret for infinitely many armed bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Infinitely many armed bandits, simple regret (bounded arms, beta-regular mean reservoir, known beta)
unmapped: New arms are drawn from an arm reservoir distribution; the mean reservoir is beta-regular at its right end point: E~' eps^beta >= P(mu > mu* - eps) >= E~ eps^beta for eps <= B~
Simple regret is measured against the right end point mu* of the mean reservoir, not the best sampled arm
Learner knows the reservoir regularity exponent beta and the bound C
settings.definition_quote: At each time $t+1$, the learner can either choose an arm $k_{t+1}$ among the set of the $K_t$ arms ... or choose to get a sample of a new arm that is generated according to $\tilde {\mathcal L}$ ... the learner has to output an arm $\widehat k \leq K_n$, and its performance is assessed by the simple regret $r_n = \bar \mu^* - \mu_{\widehat k}$

settings.name_in_paper: Infinitely many armed bandits, simple regret, arms supported on [0,1] with mu* = 1
unmapped: Arm reservoir with beta-regular mean reservoir at its end point
Right end point of the mean reservoir is mu* = 1
settings.definition_quote: the domain of the distributions of the arms are included in $[0,1]$ and where $\bar \mu^* = 1$

settings.name_in_paper: Infinitely many armed bandits, simple regret, unknown beta
unmapped: Arm reservoir with beta-regular mean reservoir at its end point
beta unknown; learner knows only a lower bound on beta
settings.definition_quote: The knowledge of $\beta$ is not anymore required, and one just needs a lower bound $\underline \beta$ on $\beta$.

results.notes: Holds with probability >= 1/3 (constant probability), recorded as high_probability. Proof uses Gaussian unit-variance arms though the class is stated for bounded arms.

results.notes: E is an unspecified large constant, hence O notation.

source.quote: Moreover, the rate $$\max\left(\frac{1}{n},\left(\tfrac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/\beta}\right),$$ is minimax-optimal for this problem, i.e.,~there exists no algorithm that achieves a better simple regret in a minimax sense.

results.notes: Stated as minimax-optimal rate; the justification in the text only yields max(1/n, n^{-1/beta}) (the log factor is not proven, cf. paper's conjecture). Probability type inherited from Theorem 1 (constant probability).
